question.text: In the pulley arrangement shown, block M hangs from a fixed pulley, while a movable pulley, suspended from the other end of the same string, carries a 3 kg block on one side and a 2 kg block on the other. Both pulleys and strings are massless, and there is no friction anywhere. Taking g = 10 m/s², find the value of M for which block M stays at rest.

figure.description: A fixed pulley is attached to a rigid support at the top. A string runs over this fixed pulley: block M hangs from one end (the left side), and the other end connects to the axle of a second, movable pulley hanging below it. A second string runs over this movable pulley, with a 3 kg block hanging from its left end and a 2 kg block hanging from its right end.

solution.approach: Require the movable pulley to stay at rest so M stays at rest, then find the tensions consistent with the motion of the 3 kg and 2 kg blocks.

steps.text: For M to stay at rest, the movable pulley below it must also stay at rest.
With the movable pulley at rest, the 3 kg and 2 kg blocks move oppositely with the same acceleration size a, both pulled by the same string tension T₂. Write Newton's second law for each.
Solve the two equations together for a and T₂.
The massless movable pulley is pulled down by T₂ from each side, so the string above it, holding M, carries twice T₂.
For M to stay at rest, its weight must equal T₁.

common_mistakes.text: Forgetting that the string above a movable pulley carries twice the tension of the string below it gives M = 2.4 kg, half the correct mass.
